description: Committee recommends $1.3 million capital project for homelessness.
Committee recommends agreement with Saskatchewan Housing Corporation.
Committee recommends pursuing additional initiative funding.

chips.text: Recommended
$1,300,000 capital project funded by Saskatchewan Housing Corporation.
Supports unsheltered homeless individuals and encampments.

description: Committee recommends $200,000 for data center regulations.
This establishes policy framework and land use rules.
Prepares city for potential future data center applications.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor Ford questioned need for study, citing unlikelihood of large data centers.
Taxpayers would fund the proposed regulatory work.
Councillor questioned if a lower-cost approach was possible for data center regulation.
Inaction could end interim bylaw, leaving no data center regulations in place.

description: Biosolids project needs R.M. of Corman Park easement by 2027.
R.M. demands $1M, Range Road 351 upgrade for easement.
Project critical for wastewater, must finish by March 2028.

chips.text: Facilitated discussions with P4G partners planned by end of 2026.

description: Pilot projects enhance safety on 23rd/3rd Avenue and 1500-20th Street.
Indigenous Support Teams provide culturally responsive safety approaches.
Engages stakeholders for 31st Street permanent shelter safety plan.

chips.text: Councillor Kelly questioned coordination with private security in safety plans.
Involves Saskatoon Public Library, City Hall security, Riversdale BID

description: New civic survey reports top concerns: housing, crime, and cost of living.
Residents rate quality of life positively, but city service satisfaction is moderate.
The new survey combines two previous ones for improved data collection.

chips.text: Annual survey cost just under $30,000.
Survey gathered input from 807 Saskatoon residents.
New survey establishes a baseline; future results will track trends.
Ward participation in the survey was imbalanced, with some oversampled.
Next civic survey planned for 2027, with minor refinements.

description: Saskatoon explores urban reserve agreements for Downtown Event District.
Negotiates municipal services, zoning with Muskeg Lake Cree Nation.

chips.text: City has no authority to regulate casino development on urban reserves.
Future agreements may include new aspects not in prior urban reserve agreements.
City's role in providing community support for urban reserve casino development is undefined.
Urban reserve creation supports Indigenous self-governance and economic development.
City commits to ongoing conversations with Muskeg Lake Cree Nation.

description: Full Link BRT launch delayed to summer 2029.
Operating costs increased to $13.5 million.
Incremental service improvements begin January 2027.
New shelters and tech will roll out earlier.

chips.text: Additional $9.2 million for operational phase-in funding in 2028-29 budget.
Administration committed to a traffic assessment for 22nd Street and Avenue W intersection.
Businesses and property owners on 20th Street (Avenue P to Whitney) are directly impacted.
Saskatoon West Business Association raised concerns about safety and traffic on 20th Street.
Administration committed to report traffic assessment results to affected businesses by Q1.

description: City to explore options for a winter daytime drop-in for men.
Report to include costs and provincial funding discussions.

chips.text: Presenters supported exploring a daytime drop-in for men.
Addresses lack of winter daytime drop-in for homeless men.

description: Delegates raise concerns about city's public engagement process.
Cite BRT projects as examples of policy shortcomings.
Call for public engagement policy review and accountability.

chips.text: Recommended
Questions raised about accessibility reviews and final design sign-off for BRT pilot station.
Delegates concerned industry input is prioritized over broader public engagement.

speakers.name: Sherry Tarasoff
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Engagement Process
said: Public engagement often falls short of the city's own policy.
Inauthentic engagement and lack of transparency erode public trust.
Accountability requires updates on engagement next steps; policy unreviewed.

description: Cary Tarasoff recommends replacing the City Manager.
Proposes current City Manager's term end May 2027.

chips.text: Recommended
Public delegate Cary Tarasoff criticized city administration's project management.

speakers.name: Cary Tarasoff
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Hiring or Re-Hiring of the City Manager
said: City administration shows poor planning and mismanagement on many projects.
Current city manager should not be re-hired; new leadership is needed.
City needs new management focus with real accountability.
